title: Contain kernel-choice boundary leakage after scheduler rebalance — post-incident action items
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: During a routine scheduler rebalance deployment on 2026-03-11 we observed a persistent p95/p99 latency regression for a subset of short-sequence chat requests and batching-sensitive endpoints. The immediate rollback restored baseline latency, but investigation revealed a subtle "boundary leakage" where the scheduler's hyperlane partitioning allowed kernels tuned for long-sequence, quantized execution to be selected for small-sequence microbatches. This caused increased kernel activation overhead, cache warmup thrash, and KV-cache misses in the short-tail workload.

What happened (high level):
- The rebalance introduced new lane boundaries ("hyperlanes") aimed at isolating heterogeneous traffic by sequence-length distribution and quantization profile.
- A race in the admission path allowed a small fraction (~0.9%) of short-sequence requests to be assigned to the wrong lane when concurrent probe windows overlapped and the lane-selection cache expired.
- Those requests used kernels optimized for large context and mixed-quant code paths; end-to-end latency for those requests spiked, and due to autoscaling hysteresis this amplified to visible p95 regression for affected customers.

Impact:
- Incident window: 2026-03-11 14:12 UTC — 2026-03-11 14:46 UTC (34 minutes).
- Affected: hosted API customers with short-sequence chat flows and high concurrency; internal SLO P95 alert fired.
- Observable: p95 increased by ~42% on affected routes, token-cost unchanged, error-rate unchanged.

How we detected it:
- Alerting: p95 tail alert fired on runtime-1.22 per-route dashboard at 14:18 UTC.
- Telemetry: sampling traces showed kernel_start_time spikes and KV-cache miss rate increase on the worker metrics.
- Initial remediation: rollback of scheduler rebalance (canary) at 14:36 UTC removed the misassignment pattern and normalized latencies by 14:46 UTC.
comments: 2026-03-11 15:00 — Diego Martinez: Rolled back scheduler rebalance; collecting traces and kube events for 14:12-14:46 window. Opening formal post-incident ticket (this).
2026-03-12 10:23 — Priya Natarajan: Verified timeline against autoscaler logs; autoscaler didn't trigger extra workers during early window, increasing per-worker microbatch pressure.
2026-03-12 17:42 — Marcus Liu: Added synthetic reproduction harness simulating mixed short/long sequence traffic with sequence-aware probes; able to reproduce 0.7-1.2% misrouting in 10k req sample.
2026-03-13 09:15 — SRE rotation: Confirmed rollback removed regressions in staging; suggested introducing selection hysteresis and TTL bump for lane-selection cache as interim mitigation.
2026-03-14 11:50 — Diego Martinez: Drafted patch that gates kernel selection with a grace window and enforces lane affinity for warm KVs; running unit and integration tests.
2026-03-14 12:30 — PM: Noted customer comms plan and preparing targeted outreach for affected tenants.
action_items: AI-1: Implement selection hysteresis — add 200ms grace period after lane transition during which lane-selection favors existing worker lane to avoid probe overlap misassignments. Owner: Diego Martinez. ETA: 2026-03-20.
AI-2: Increase lane-selection cache TTL from 50ms to 300ms with jitter to reduce concurrent expirations. Owner: Marcus Liu. ETA: 2026-03-18.
AI-3: Introduce deterministic lane-affinity hashes for short-sequence routes as a safety net (route-level opt-in). Owner: Priya Natarajan. ETA: 2026-03-25.
AI-4: Add regression test to CI: mixed-traffic soak test that runs for 30 minutes under realistic concurrency and validates per-route p95 within 10% of baseline. Owner: Marcus Liu. ETA: 2026-03-22.

AI-5: Add targeted telemetry and alerts: kernel_mismatch_rate and lane-selection_misassignment_rate with page-level thresholds; dashboard tile and runbook update. Owner: SRE team (oncall: Jordan Park). ETA: 2026-03-17.
AI-6: Canary rollout plan for the hysteresis + TTL changes: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across regions with p95 guardrails and abort conditions. Owner: Diego Martinez. ETA: start 2026-03-21.
AI-7: Post-deploy verification: synthetic benchmark and real-traffic shadowing for 48 hours post-100% rollout. Owner: Performance SIG (leads: Avery Chen). ETA: complete by 2026-04-15.
AI-8: Customer outreach: targeted email to affected tenants explaining root cause, rollback, and upcoming fixes. Owner: Customer Success (contact: Elise Gomez). ETA: 2026-03-16.

AI-9: Long-term: evaluate architectural options to decouple lane boundaries from transient probe state by persisting minimal lane assignment hints in worker-local metadata and exposing a stable admission token. Owner: Architecture (lead: Rohit Verma). ETA: RFC by 2026-04-30.
AI-10: Security/Compliance review: ensure no sensitive keys are leaked by expanded telemetry; add review step to release checklist. Owner: Security (lead: Nina Kaur). ETA: 2026-03-19.
reproduction_notes: Repro harness: use bench/traffic-mix with 80% short sequences (<=64 tokens) and 20% long sequences (>=2048 tokens) at concurrency 250 across 8 workers. Introduce periodic probe bursts (every 7s) and randomize probe window by +/-50ms to emulate race conditions. Observed misassignment frequency 0.6-1.2% and correlated KV-cache miss increase. Repro script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-tests/compare/hyperlane-probe-repro (branch: hyperlane-probe-repro).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Deploy hysteresis + TTL changes via canary; verify p95 for short-sequence routes returns to baseline within 5% at 10% canary and remains stable at each rollout step.
AC-2: New alerts (kernel_mismatch_rate) fire only on true misassignments and have <1% false-positive rate in 7-day validation window.
AC-3: Regression CI test passes consistently for 10 consecutive runs in CI pipeline.
AC-4: Customer outreach executed and affected customers acknowledge remediation plan or are offered follow-up support.
